text:
tim_acme: Hey team — ran into a weird one. Our org hit monthly credits at 00:00 UTC but a long‑running Jupyter notebook session kept streaming and is still showing 0 credits in the UI, streaming calls started failing with 429s a few minutes later. Repro steps below.

ash_support: sorry about that, can you paste the org id and the root request id from one of the 429s?

tim_acme: org: acme-inc-prod, sample request id: r-0a1b2c3d4e, timestamp 2025-11-25T00:03:12Z. The notebook had an open websocket connection established before midnight and then kept calling the streaming endpoint.

ash_support: got it. a couple quick questions — is the notebook using a single long‑lived API key or rotating tokens? and are you seeing UI show 0 immediately at midnight or a gap?

tim_acme: single API key bound to service user. UI showed 0 at 00:00:00 UTC, but the websocket didn't error until ~00:03 and then 429s. UI refresh/relogin still showed 0.

infra-bot: Automated check: org=acme-inc-prod credits_current=0 credits_reset_at=2025-11-25T00:00:00Z last_charge=2025-11-24T23:59:58Z

mike_eng_infra: thanks — this looks like the classic in‑flight session visibility problem. Long lived connections may have local token caches (client or proxy). Can you share the websocket client logs around the 00:00 boundary and the exact streaming request payload (headers ok to redact except x-request-id)?

tim_acme: pasted logs (redacted):
```
[2025-11-25T00:00:01Z] ws: send chunk seq=214 size=512
[2025-11-25T00:02:59Z] ws: recv 200 partial chunk
[2025-11-25T00:03:12Z] http: POST /v1/stream 429 x-request-id=r-0a1b2c3d4e body="quota_exhausted"
```

ash_support: thanks. can you run a quick API check from the same environment to confirm what the server reports for credits? run: 
```
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" "https://api.redwood.com/v1/orgs/acme-inc-prod/credits" | jq
```

tim_acme: ran it. response (redacted):
```
{"credits":0, "reset_at":"2025-11-25T00:00:00Z", "window":"monthly"}
```

elaine_billing: FYI: billing shows normal behavior — monthly bucket rolled at midnight UTC for this tenant. No prorate or topup happened.

mike_eng_infra: likely sequence: 1) credits reset at 00:00, 2) server accepted in‑flight websocket frames while KV cache allowed short grace, 3) subsequent token accounting hits quota and returns 429. We need to confirm if streaming continuations are charged against the new window immediately or if there's a short server‑side allowance.

ash_support: action items: (a) support to collect full websocket handshake + client library version, (b) infra to check if any grace window is applied to in‑flight sessions, (c) recommend customer workaround: rotate/refresh session after reset to pick up new credit state.

mike_eng_infra: infra check shows no intentional grace period — charging is immediate at reset. However we do have one edge case: cached auth tokens in the request path (gateway/local proxy) can buffer requests for a few seconds and make accounting appear delayed. We're going to search logs for r-0a1b2c3d4e across gateways.

infra-bot: Gateway trace: r-0a1b2c3d4e seen on gw-3 at 2025-11-25T00:03:12Z forwarded to stream-srv-7 where quota check returned 429. No replayed requests earlier.

tim_acme: quick question — is reconnecting the websocket enough to resume usage once we top up? or do we need to create a new API key?

ash_support: reconnect should pick up the fresh credit state. If you top up while session is open, recommend reconnecting the session within ~10s.

tim_acme: tried reconnect after manual topup — reconnecting fixed it, stream resumed. thanks. :relieved:

elaine_billing: note for records: customer performed manual topup at 00:05 UTC, amount +5000 tokens, invoice id topup-9921.

mike_eng_infra: we'll file a short postmortem note: reproduce with long‑running client that buffers frames across reset and confirm whether we need UI hint or automatic session invalidation on reset. Tentative root cause: immediate charging at reset + client/gateway buffering led to delayed 429s.

ash_support: closing loop — tim, we'll follow up with a tiny change: recommend adding an ephemeral session TTL or auto‑reconnect guidance in doc. if you want us to dig deeper into gateway buffering we can escalate.

tim_acme: please escalate — want to avoid customer impact during demos. also adding reconnection step to runbook now. thanks everyone.

ash_support: noted, escalating to eng‑infra for deeper trace correlation. :thumbsup:
